memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Season all your grain offerings with salt. Do not leave the salt of the covenant of your God out of your grain offerings; add salt to all your offerings.'" - Lev 2:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God says it three times in one verse. Add salt. Do not leave it out. Add salt to all your offerings.

Salt was the opposite of yeast. Yeast ferments and spoils; salt preserves and keeps. In the ancient world, sharing salt sealed an agreement — it signified something durable, something that would not decay. That is why God calls it the salt of the covenant.

So every grain offering carried a small reminder that God's covenant with His people did not spoil, sour, or expire. However often the Israelite failed, God's commitment held.

That has not changed. God's covenant faithfulness is the same today, secured now in the new covenant sealed by Christ's own blood (Lk 22:20). Paul was certain that God is faithful even when we are faithless, for he cannot disown himself (2 Tim 2:13).

Jesus later told His followers, "You are the salt of the earth" (Mtt 5:13). Believers are meant to have that same preserving, enduring quality in a world that spoils quickly — and Paul urges that our conversation always be seasoned with salt (Col 4:6).

Do not offer God a faith that goes flat. Salt it with covenant confidence.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I rest in God's covenant faithfulness, or in my own consistency?
2. Where could my presence have a preserving effect this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your covenant does not spoil with time. Make my life salty — enduring, faithful, and preserving good wherever You place me. Amen.
